extensions.name: Nimora
extensions.description: Live and upcoming sports, movie and TV catalogs, plus anime streams, running as a JavaScript bundle in the sandboxed QuickJS runtime.
extensions.author: nimbusfvck
releaseNotes: Nimora 2.0.2: added TVNow live channel catalogs with category shelves, category-specific See more filtering, and an EPG-backed channel schedule; removed the legacy fixture timeline catalog.
Nimora 2.0.1: marked FCTV events older than the live window as ended instead of incorrectly showing them as upcoming.

Nimora 2.0.0: added Sports Matches to Home and the All category with uncapped See more navigation, hardened Football Highlights playback for current multi-iframe embeds, and added the FCTV33 live-event source.
Added the Sports Matches catalog to the All category so Asian Games 2026 appears on Home with its full uncapped item list and See more navigation.
Fixed browser-only TimStreams embeds such as Stan Sport by capturing their HLS request in a headless WebView and returning it to native playback without opening the visible Cloudflare browser.
Probe the full DaddyLive event channel list lazily, using three concurrent checks and stopping as soon as three playable sources are found.
Start live playback from the first playable provider, keep slower providers as background fallbacks, and make DaddyLive and Cloudflare-blocked channels fail fast.
Refresh DaddyLive playback URLs on every renewal while deduplicating only concurrent resolves, so expired live tokens are not reused.
Reduced the Sports catalog upcoming window to three days and limited FotMob date fetches accordingly, with Roxie and TimStreams using the same window.
Fixed DaddyLive schedule grouping for crowded events so channels map to the correct football match before HLS validation.
Avoided opening the Cloudflare WebView for VidCore and skip VidCore quickly when its page is blocked; VidRock now rejects unavailable HLS playlists before playback fallback.
Added VidCore as a multi-resolution HLS provider with Wyzie subtitle enrichment and reordered VOD provider priority based on observed resolve speed.
Added VidFast as a fresh multi-resolution HLS provider with server fallback and optional subtitle tracks.
Probe the first five DaddyLive channels in parallel and return up to three with a validated HLS playlist and media segment.
Added DaddyLive channel streams to FotMob events and validated the HLS playlist and first media segment before playback.
Matched TimStreams football events to FotMob by event ID so alternate team names do not create duplicate cards under Other Leagues.
Moved CDNLiveTV event-feed requests out of Home catalog refresh while keeping CDNLiveTV available as an on-demand stream provider.
Removed the Live category; Sports is the only sports category.
Hid the Live category from Nimora catalogs; Compact kept its separate Schedule category.
Added Sports as a league-grouped row catalog, improved football name matching, and hid ended matches from the Sport catalog.
Added a minimum TMDB rating of 6 to the Korean Series row so low-rated or unrated titles are excluded.
Improved Indonesian Movies and Korean movie/series rows by removing the 180-day cutoff, and increased TMDB poster artwork to w780 for sharper mobile heroes.
Fixed Football Highlights pagination so the All-category shelf collects enough playable posts for See more.
Added TMDB list metadata for overview, original titles and languages, genres, countries, and rating vote counts.
Fixed Febbox quality switching so 1080p remains available after selecting 720p or 360p, and deduplicated cached source labels during refresh.
Restored Febbox 360p and 720p variants when quality playlists are individually returned as HLS masters, and simplified the source label to the provider name.
Added TimStreams live-event sources and reused its event artwork in the existing sports catalog while preserving FotMob as football metadata authority.
Restored Football Highlights on Home and the All category by wiring the Time Soccer catalog bridge.
Restored Febbox fixed-quality variants so 720p and 360p remain available alongside the adaptive HLS source.
Grouped Febbox quality links into one Auto source with fixed resolutions as playback variants, while keeping master HLS adaptive.
Split Febbox quality playlists into independently selectable sources while refreshing signed URLs on resolve.
Kept Febbox master HLS playlists intact for native adaptive quality; fixed-quality playlists remain selectable variants.
Kept All-category search on TMDB and made Anime search AniList-first with Sokuja fallback when AniList errors.
Changed Febbox quality links into variants on one source, preserving 2160p/1080p/720p choices while keeping startup quality selection lightweight.
Removed TMDB from the AniList anime detail path; episode titles, thumbnails, trailers, and related anime collections now come directly from AniList.
Fixed Febbox source discovery by using the file fid and prioritizing signed quality-list HLS URLs before legacy playback fallbacks.
Fixed Febbox quality resolution by sending the share key and accepting the top-level quality HTML returned by Febbox.
Fixed AniSkip markers for AniList episodes mapped through TMDB seasons by querying the absolute anime episode number.
Fixed Febbox playback by resolving the signed HLS URL through the player endpoint, forwarding the personal ui cookie only to Febbox, and rejecting invalid HLS responses.
Made long-running anime details load TMDB seasons lazily, while preserving absolute episode mapping for playback and subtitles across multi-season anime such as One Piece.
Added the Febbox provider with direct ShowBox-to-Febbox HLS resolution, optional personal ui cookie forwarding only to Febbox, fresh signed URLs, and 4K rendition discovery.
Added KickassAnime as an HLS anime source with fresh iOS-compatible playback resolution, subtitle tracks, and season-safe matching.

Made AniList anime details TMDB-first for richer metadata, episode titles, and per-episode artwork; preserved AniList episode refs and absolute multi-season mapping so long-running anime such as One Piece continue matching Sokuja and Indomax.

Routed TMDB requests through the private Cloudflare proxy with edge caching and server-side key rotation, so AniList episode details can load TMDB still artwork without exposing API keys in the bundle; AniList cover/banner artwork remains the fallback.
Centralized TMDB API requests with key rotation across available keys so anime artwork and metadata survive stale or rate-limited keys.
Moved All-category anime rankings to AniList with Sokuja fallback and added lazy TMDB episode still artwork for AniList anime details.
Added persistent AniList caching, duplicate-request coalescing, and a conservative 75-request-per-minute guard to stay below AniList's 90-request limit.
Switched the Anime category to AniList-first data with Sokuja fallback and added a minimum TMDB vote count of 10 for Korean Series.
Sorted Korean Movies and Korean Series by TMDB rating, using popularity as the tie-breaker.
Switched the Indonesian Movies category row to Indomax's rated country catalog with direct detail metadata and playback refs, while retaining TMDB fallback.
Prioritized rated Indonesian and Korean movie rows plus Korean Series by TMDB daily Trending Today rankings, with rated non-trending titles kept as fallback.
Disabled the Idlix stream provider while its upstream API is blocked by a Cloudflare challenge; added HD TMDB alternate backdrops and restored TMDB title logos for the Featured Summary.
Fixed See more pagination for Indonesian and Korean movie/series rows and limited country movie rows to TMDB digital releases without vote-count filtering.
Added recent Indonesian and Korean movie rows plus recent Korean series, without vote-count filtering; removed Indonesian Series from the category layout.
Added Trending Today rows to the Movie, TV Shows, and Anime categories; Movie and TV use TMDB daily trends, while Anime uses Sokuja's weekly ranking.
Changed the Sokuja Anime category to show Most Popular, Most Rating, Most Recent, and genre shelves together as separate rows.
Removed the Movie/TV grid catalog and improved Movie, TV, and Sokuja Anime sections with popularity, rating, recent, and genre browsing.
Updated Movie and TV category sections to Most Popular, Most Rating, Most Recent, and TMDB genre rows.
Fixed Savefilm Abyss player 3 playback by rebuilding fresh `/sora` MP4 URLs and preserving 360p, 720p, and 1080p variants.
Changed Hydrax Auto startup to the highest validated rendition up to 720p while keeping higher qualities available for manual selection.
Added Idlix movie and TV episode streams using Nimora's existing titles, with fresh gate/session resolution and subtitles.
Added CDNLiveTV event discovery and fresh HLS channel resolution.
Removed Featured Sports from the all category; it remains available only to Home's Featured Hero.
Fixed the Featured Sports catalog registration so Home's Featured Hero loads it without rendering an erroneous Home shelf.
Added a Featured Sports catalog so highly rated upcoming football big matches can enter Home's Featured Hero before kickoff without being marked live.
Renamed the Nimora matches catalog label from Live Now to Sports Matches to distinguish it from the Home live shelf.
Removed Jikan completely, including its anime provider, anime shelves, alias lookups, and health probes.
Switched Motorsport catalog data back to RoxieStreams so live and recently finished events remain available in the timeline; SPOTV is no longer used for catalog data.
Removed the Live Now shelf from the All category; live events remain available through the Live timeline.
Removed Jikan completely, including its anime provider, anime shelves, alias lookups, and health probes.
Made SPOTV the authoritative Motorsport catalog source with current timestamps and artwork; Cricfy, PlayZTV, and RoxieStreams remain stream resolvers with kickoff-based matching.
Removed stale or duplicate generic Motorsport catalog rows so events such as MotoGP use SPOTV's schedule and live state.
Added Roxie Fighting and Motorsports page feeds so current UFC, boxing, MXGP, MotoGP, NASCAR, and related events appear in Nimora.
Removed the global Schedule category, kept Live as a timeline, and filtered stale Cricfy events after their sport-specific expiry window.
Removed FCTV33, kept finished FotMob matches in Schedule as ended, and prevented stale provider events from reappearing in Live Now.
Fixed duplicate football matches caused by abbreviated provider team names, renamed the Home live shelf to Live Now, and renamed the Sport category to Schedule.
Added RoxieStreams as a source-only sports provider: its countdown determines live/upcoming status, unmatched events can be added, and FotMob remains the Football SSOT.
Disabled FCTV33 Live Events because its provider CDN rejects the app playback path with HTTP 403.
Fixed FCTV playback by matching the APK web token flow: decoding obfuscated stream URLs, creating the rb-session AES-CTR token URL, validating playlist media, and retrying fallback edges.

Fixed FCTV live playback by validating playlist media segments before returning a source, retrying fresh signed stream details, filtering Sorotan items, and showing tournament names on live event cards.
Added FCTV33 live-event fallback streams and provider-only football events to Live, while keeping FotMob as the Football schedule source.
Added separate horizontal Movie and TV shelves to their category pages, including Top By Genre rows, while keeping mixed shelves on Home.
Fixed League Channels returning empty in the live catalog when the PlayZTV category feed is loaded through the published bundle.
Added League Channels to Live with Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Champions League, and Europa League shelves sourced from channel links in PlayZTV and Cricfy.
Hardened the Jikan anime catalog against upstream 504s with persistent cache, serialized requests, retries, and stale-data fallback while reducing the initial All-category request burst.

Added cached cross-source anime title aliases from MAL/Jikan and Anime Relations Mapping, so Sokuja, Indomax, LayarKaca, and Savefilm can search alternate anime names automatically for both series and episodes.
Fixed LK21 movie matching so a partial title such as Dreams cannot select a different movie such as Train Dreams, and renamed the TMDB popularity shelves to Popular Movies and Popular TV Series.
Fixed LK21 ratings so they appear on both catalog cards and detail pages.
Changed the All Time movie and series shelves to popularity rankings and moved Oscar Nominees and Cannes Film Festival to the bottom of Home.
Restored the Coming Soon Home shelf and fixed Movies on LK21 pagination so additional pages load correctly.
Removed the Coming Soon shelf from Home.
Fixed Cricfy football source matching when the provider abbreviates team names, including Atl. Madrid for Atlético Madrid.
Fixed Sokuja quality mapping so each episode exposes one source with its available 480p, 720p, and 1080p playback variants.
Fixed PlayZTV current-feed decoding and endpoint fallback, restored Cricfy in Compact, and hardened Sokuja artwork and episode-date parsing.
Moved the Anime catalog and Home anime shelves to Sokuja, adding Sokuja's Top Anime All Time and Popular Anime This Week rankings while retaining AniList metadata for existing references.
Made Premier League Shorts follow FotMob's current season and matchweek, merging active and latest-played Clipro feeds so new matchweek moments keep appearing automatically.

Consolidated the public catalog providers into Movie & Series, Anime, Live Sport & Event, NSFW, and Shorts; Dracin, UEFA, Premier League, and TMDB preview feeds now remain internal contributors to their logical catalog.
Moved the LayarKaca catalog to the All category with separate Movies on LK21 and TV Series on LK21 sections; the TV section uses Series Unggulan.
Added PlayZTV as an independent live-event stream provider with fresh link and token resolution, so it can be enabled separately from other stream providers.
Changed the LayarKaca catalog to a compact Home shelf section so movie and TV catalogs remain visible together; the full catalog is still available through See more.

Added an independent LayarKaca catalog for films and series. LayarKaca catalog and stream providers can now be enabled separately, with catalog series retaining direct episode playback through LayarKaca streams.
Added Dramadev as a stream-only movie source for TMDB movies, with exact title matching and fresh HLS resolution while keeping Dracin catalog playback intact.
Curated UEFA Champions League and Premier League Shorts to the 20 newest playable items and added movie, TV and football tags for Shorts filtering.
Added paginated Dramaverse and Storyreel Shorts catalogs with per-item tags and episode playback through fresh HLS resolution.
Restored Hydrax quality variants from decoder responses and updated P2P Playcdn resolution for the current `/verify/{slug}` flow.
Made Hydrax start playback from the lowest validated quality by default while keeping the quality variants ordered from highest to lowest for manual selection.
Fixed LayarKaca TurboVIP resolution by retrying the parent watch page and capturing the nested EmTurbovid player before WebView timeout.
Exposed title logos for all TMDB Trending Movie and TV catalog items with bounded, memoized artwork lookups.
Curated Football to include Saudi Pro League and exclude UEFA Youth League.
Fixed football league icons by using FotMob's canonical league artwork and primary competition IDs, including Champions League.
Fixed Champions League fixtures disappearing when FotMob uses season-specific league IDs and primary competition IDs.
Fixed LayarKaca `/iframe3/` resolution by parsing the nested player after a browser/Cloudflare fetch, avoiding parent-page timeouts while preserving source and quality extraction.
Fixed Hydrax `/sora` extensionless media URLs being reported as `other` instead of explicit MP4.
Fixed Hydrax playback by rebuilding CloudStream's encrypted `/sora` MP4 URLs and preserving 360p, 480p, 720p, and 1080p quality variants.
Fixed LayarKaca browser-only `/iframe3/` players by resolving the nested player from the parent watch page when the direct endpoint is blocked or empty.
Aligned LayarKaca resolution with Nuvio's extractor flow by prioritizing embedded player iframes and decoding packed Abyss/Filemoon JWPlayer configs into validated HLS streams.
Hardened LayarKaca player extraction against Cloudflare redirects to the catalog homepage and invalid placeholder URLs before they reach the resolver.
Fixed LayarKaca P2P Videonode resolution by using the normal HTTP-first extraction path so nested player iframes can resolve without waiting for a WebView timeout.
Fixed Hydrax WebView resolution to stay on the Abyss quality chain instead of falling back to a single Playcdn rendition, including support for `abyss.to` player links.
Fixed Hydrax WebView resolution to prefer the Abyss player quality payload before falling back to the single Playcdn HLS rendition, allowing the available fixed quality variants to reach the player.

Fixed Hydrax fixed-MP4 quality variants by joining each rendition's media host and path, filtering AV1-only entries, and exposing valid H264 480p, 720p, and 1080p streams to the player quality picker.
Added independent LayarKaca HYDRAX, P2P, TURBOVIP, and CAST sources with Indonesian locale metadata and runtime movie-domain discovery through d21.team.
Exposed Hydrax's fixed 360p, 480p, 720p, and 1080p renditions as real playback variants instead of claiming a quality from a single URL.
Hardened LayarKaca player extraction across Filesim, Playcdn, Videonode, Abyss, and browser-only fallbacks while preserving required referers.
Added FlyStream leak metadata to TMDB details: `On Digital` and `Leak` tags plus parsed digital release dates.
Fixed Cricfy extensionless playlist streams by detecting HLS or DASH from the playback response instead of relying on a URL extension.
Fixed Savefilm native playback by extracting AceFile's direct Google Drive MP4 mirror and filtering Abyss browser-only `.fd` chunks.
Fixed Savefilm playback when Abyss player pages hide MP4 sources behind a JavaScript redirect and AES-CTR encrypted payload.
Fixed Savefilm catalog items using the provider's original title so source lookup still works after the app restores a cached item.
Fixed Savefilm Adult catalog loading by keeping provider-private detail URLs out of the strict catalog item protocol.

Fixed Savefilm NSFW source lookup when TMDB's title differs from Savefilm's article title by preserving the detail URL, supporting current headline markup, and resolving relative player tabs correctly.
Fixed Savefilm stream discovery: the provider now scans all Muvipro player tabs, decodes packed player configurations, and exposes direct HLS/MP4 sources with the required referer headers.

Fixed Indomax anime episode matching so year-suffixed search results do not select a same-title movie, and expanded NSFW source discovery to scan all player tabs including Peytonepre and IPlayerHLS fallback streams.
Follow Indomax's final redirect URL and probe the rotating `akses1`–`akses10` mirrors so the NSFW catalog survives mirror rotation.
Added an active Indomax catalog mirror fallback so the NSFW catalog still loads when `idmxl.ink` returns a blocked response before redirecting.
Changed Savefilm to an NSFW catalog-only provider: matched titles now use TMDB refs so the regular movie/TV stream providers handle playback, while Indomax keeps its own NSFW catalog and streams.
Refined the Savefilm health smoke to validate a current homepage movie through its active player tab and TurboVidHLS HLS playlist.
Fixed the Savefilm source health smoke to follow the active homepage movie and its `?player=N` tabs before validating the TurboVidHLS HLS playlist.
Added Savefilm Adult to the NSFW catalog and Savefilm movie/series source resolution through TurboVidHLS HLS streams, including paginated listings and series episode guides.
Fixed Dracin Shorts items being discarded by the app because episode metadata was missing its protocol-v2 parent reference.
Put Dracin Shorts ahead of TMDB in the Shorts feed so the first item is no longer a TMDB coming-soon title.
Hardened the KlikXXi Dracin release health smoke to try every player tab and select a supported Hexload stream when the first tab uses another server.
Added Dracin Shorts from KlikXXi: the latest portrait episodes are exposed as Shorts items and resolved through Muvipro AJAX to direct Hexload MP4 streams, with provider-specific health coverage.
Replaced the all-time popular movie and series shelves with Top Movies All Time and Top Series All Time, ranked by TMDB rating with a minimum of 1,000 votes.

Added paginated Popular Movies All Time and Popular Series All Time shelves, lowered the Korean and Indonesian shelf vote threshold to 5, and added movie collection metadata above recommendations in detail.
Switched TMDB detail recommendations to the dedicated recommendations endpoint, with similar titles retained only as a fallback.
Added partial source discovery: playback starts from the first non-empty provider result while the complete provider fan-out continues in the background for source switching and fallback.
Reduced FlyStream to one de-duplicated highest-quality source per title while keeping the source label generic so quality remains a player-level choice.

Added external subtitle lookup for AniList episodes: Nimora maps the selected AniList episode through FlyStream's identity route, then fetches Shegu's direct subtitle tracks for the mapped TMDB season and episode.

Fixed Sokuja returning no source for AniList episodes whose title is only `Shingeki no Kyojin`: a season-qualified Sokuja result such as `Shingeki no Kyojin Season 1` is now accepted even when AniList provides no episode air date.

Fixed Attack on Titan episodes returning no anime sources: Sokuja now accepts its season-qualified title (`Shingeki no Kyojin Season 1`), and FlyStream resolves AniList episode IDs through its identity mapping before requesting streams.

Removed MeteGol's fake per-stream quality claims: AlAngulo and FutbolLibre both printed the same "720p" on every single channel regardless of what actually played, so the label no longer states a quality the source never measured. Merged stream labels now also tag their origin site (Agenda18/AlAngulo/FutbolLibre/Deporflix), so identically named channels pulled from different sources under the same fixture (e.g. two "Disney+" entries) are no longer indistinguishable. Deporflix and FutbolLibre are disabled for now: Deporflix for its two-request chain and loose title matching, FutbolLibre for mostly relabeling AlAngulo's own channel pool (la18hd.su, streamtp-golden1.click) under a second near-identical name while covering fewer matches and streams.

Fixed episodes offering the skip-intro button twice: AniSkip carries several community submissions per episode, and overlapping ones were all kept, so skipping landed inside the next intro and offered the button again. Overlapping segments of the same kind now collapse to the earliest, and an outro sitting inside an opening is dropped rather than letting the player treat the first minutes as the end of the episode.

Reordered the movie and TV sources so VaPlayer and vidrock lead, FlyStream follows for the 4K ladder nothing else offers, and VidEasy trails after most of its entries failed to resolve; FlyStream's label no longer carries the ladder's top rung, which named a rendition the player does not open.
Added the protocol-v2 segments role backed by IntroDB for TMDB episodes and AniSkip for AniList anime episodes.
Added FlyStream as the first movie/TV source with fresh session-gated adaptive HLS resolution, and expanded source health checks to cover provider-specific endpoints and smoke flows.

Switched FotMob's popular league curation to the US market while retaining Indonesian match localization and the WIB calendar, preventing domestic Indonesian competitions from being promoted into Football.

Fixed Cricfy sources duplicating after refresh by keeping source IDs stable across token changes, and added the Deportivo A Coruña/Deportivo La Coruña football-name alias so MeteGol can match the fixture.
Removed redundant Al Angulo and Futbol Libre prefixes from stream labels and de-duplicated identical MeteGol stream URLs.

Expanded MeteGol football streams with Al Angulo, Futbol Libre, and Deporflix, preserving FotMob as the fixture catalog, per-source playback referers, and fresh token resolution; stream labels now show the source name without a redundant MeteGol prefix.

Added MeteGol's agenda18 football stream provider: it matches the agenda to FotMob fixtures, keeps the parsed schedule across launches when `host.storage` is available, and resolves fresh HLS playback URLs when a source is selected.

Kept Cricfy events and sources working while its API is slow or refusing: the event schedule is now requested with a longer timeout and kept between app launches, so a cold start serves the stored schedule straight away and refreshes it in the background instead of showing an empty Live row while the upstream stalls. Needs an app build that provides extension storage; on an older build nothing changes.
Kora now resolves a repeated source through a different edge each time, so retrying after a live stall takes another route instead of pinning to the one that just stalled.
Added paginated See more loading for TMDB Highlights backed by TMDB pages, including Korean and Indonesian shelves, Top Rated, Popular Today, and streaming-provider rows.
Added Popular Korean and Popular Indonesian Series & Movies shelves to TMDB Highlights, using popularity-ranked country filters with a reusable configuration for adding more countries later.
Removed finished football matches from the schedule takeout so completed fixtures no longer appear in `Today` or the upcoming Football shelf.
Fixed the women-only exclusion to detect women's competitions from the league name, including FotMob's `UEFA Women's Europa Cup`, even when club names do not carry a `(W)` suffix.
Fixed popular and international football curation to match league IDs only, preventing unrelated competitions with the same display name (such as Liviy Bereh vs Karpaty) from appearing.

Refined football fixture visibility using FotMob's `popular` and `international` league lists, removing noisy unlisted competitions while keeping the daily `/matches` feed, large club crests, and 433 league branding.

Switched football fixtures to FotMob's daily matches endpoint for schedule and live status, restoring matches missing from the TV guide such as Bournemouth vs Everton and Elversberg vs Leverkusen; all leagues are now shown, with large FotMob club crests and 433 league logos.

Fixed a live match staying marked as scheduled no matter how many times the app refreshed, e.g. Liverpool vs Nottingham Forest: FotMob spells some clubs differently in its schedule feed than by433 does in its live feed (e.g. "Nottm Forest" vs "Nottingham Forest"), so by433's live confirmation silently failed to match, and FotMob's own schedule fetch — which often carries no `isLive` flag at all — is cached for 15 minutes regardless of how often the app asks. Reconciles the known abbreviation variants.
Added competition branding to football event payloads: FotMob league colors and logos now reach the app so match banners can use the competition's visual identity.

Fixed Time Soccer highlights loading slowly and stalling on every quality switch: resolution (post, embed, playlist validation) spoofed a browser User-Agent throughout, but the resolved stream handed to the player carried no headers at all, so its own segment fetches fell back to the platform default UA — a mismatch a CDN that treats non-browser clients differently wouldn't show until real playback started. Playback now sends the same User-Agent resolution already used successfully.

Removed Football Highlights from the Shorts previews feed (added in 0.6.72): landscape recap footage doesn't fit Shorts' vertical format, and the clip a viewer would preview there is already the whole thing, not a lead-in to watch something bigger. The Football Highlights row on Home/Sport is unaffected.
Added a Football Highlights row to Home's Highlights shelf, sourced from Time Soccer alongside Trending Movie/TV and Popular Today.
Added Football Highlights to the Shorts previews feed: a highlight clip is already short-form, so its preview is the same Videa HLS stream full playback resolves, not a separate trailer lookup.

The `previews` catalog now checks every candidate for a resolvable YouTube trailer before including it, instead of leaving that to the app's own lazy per-item resolution — a title TMDB has no trailer for used to make it into the Shorts feed anyway, only to get skipped the instant the viewer swiped to it. The per-item trailer lookup this uses is cached, so resolving playback for the same title later doesn't repeat the fetch.
Added a Time Soccer TV football highlights catalog to Home and Sport, with Videa HLS playback and paginated See more loading so the catalog can continue beyond the initial batch.

Added a `previews` catalog to TMDB — Coming Soon interleaved two-to-one with released Trending Movie/TV, de-duplicated by ref — and a lightweight per-item trailer resolver (official Trailer, then official Teaser, then a non-official Trailer, then the newest video) that fetches only `/movie|tv/{id}/videos` per candidate instead of the full detail payload. This is the data source for the app's new Shorts feed; it does not change anything on Home.

Fixed Coming Soon still missing far-out tentpoles like Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday even after 0.6.67 started discovering them: the shelf re-sorted the combined movie/TV pool by nearest release date and cut it to 25, which buried a title releasing months out under an entire page of smaller titles releasing sooner. Coming Soon now ranks the merged pool by popularity, matching what each source query already used to decide who's in it.

Brought back Coming Soon, sourced properly this time: `/movie/upcoming` only covers the next month or two of theatrical releases, so a tentpole releasing later in the year (e.g. Dune: Part Three, Avengers: Doomsday) never appeared even though it's clearly upcoming. Movies and TV are now discovered by future release date and ranked by popularity instead, so the shelf leads with titles people actually anticipate rather than whichever small release happens to land soonest — while still dropping anything whose date turns out not to be genuinely in the future.

Removed the Coming Soon row: after filtering out titles TMDB misclassifies as upcoming (0.6.65), the region's genuinely future-dated catalog was thin enough on most days that the shelf wasn't worth a permanent spot on Home. Movie and TV items still carry their release date individually, so a title that isn't out yet still shows as upcoming wherever it appears (e.g. Trending) with the same Remind Me behavior.

Fixed Coming Soon showing titles that already released, such as Terminator and Avengers: Endgame: TMDB can list a title in `/movie/upcoming` (or `/discover/tv`) for reasons other than a genuine future release — e.g. a theatrical rerelease window — while the release date field we read and display still carries the original, long-past date. Coming Soon now re-checks that date itself and drops anything that isn't actually in the future, instead of trusting TMDB's own classification.

Added a release date to movie and TV catalog items and a new Coming Soon row (movies from `/movie/upcoming`, TV series from `/discover/tv` filtered to future air dates, both merged and ordered by how soon each one releases), so the app can flag titles that aren't out yet and let you get reminded before they are.

Fixed Home's Sport category still showing the Football shelf in editorial/league order (e.g. Real Madrid leading regardless of kickoff) even though the dedicated Football subcategory page ("See more") was already chronological — every football listing now sorts by kickoff, not just the one reached by drilling in.

Fixed live football matches disappearing from the Live category and Featured Hero whenever by433's live feed didn't happen to cover them: FotMob's own `isLive` flag is now trusted on its own within a plausible match window, instead of always requiring by433 confirmation.
Kept a match relevant for a day after kickoff instead of dropping it the moment it finished, so yesterday's results still show under their own "Yesterday" date section.

Treated England's EFL Cup (Carabao Cup / League Cup) as an important competition, like the existing Super Cup exception, since FotMob's account-localized "popular" league list leaves it out for most countries.

Fixed Cricfy events being memoized for the entire app session with no expiry: a fixture added to Cricfy's events list after the first fetch never got sources and never appeared under Live, no matter how many times the app was refreshed.
Added an alias for Athletic Club (Athletic Bilbao) so its official name no longer collapses to the bare, ambiguous "athletic" and fails to match Cricfy's own spelling of the team.

Grouped the Football section by kickoff day (Today, Tomorrow, then date) instead of by league, so a fixture kicking off soon no longer trails one still days away just because of league order in the feed.
Added a Popular Anime This Season row to Home, sourced from AniList's current season and sorted by popularity.
The anime grid no longer repeats the shelf name as a section heading.
Anime no longer appears twice on Home: TMDB's trending rows leave Japanese animation to the Trending Anime row.

Moved anime to AniList: the anime category, anime search when the Search screen is scoped to it, and Home's anime row, now called Trending Anime. AniList lists each cour as its own entry, numbered the way Sokuja and Indomax number them, so more episodes find a source. The separate Indomax Anime catalog is gone; Indomax still supplies streams.

Fixed Sokuja returning no sources for series older than the site, such as One Piece: episode matching no longer requires the site's upload date to equal the TMDB air date, and TMDB's arc-sized seasons are mapped onto Sokuja's absolute episode numbering.
Sokuja now discovers its current streaming domain at runtime from its landing hosts, so anime sources keep working when the mirror rotates instead of failing until the next release.
Ignored invalid Cricfy event and participant artwork URLs so malformed upstream images no longer break sports catalogs.
Filtered live football events to popular leagues, including by433 live matches matched by league name, while preserving friendly and Super Cup exceptions.
Kept provider-native subtitles on resolved sources and moved Shegu lookups to the explicit external-subtitles flow.
Split football schedule and live status: FotMob TV guide supplies the seven-day schedule, while by433's live feed drives the refreshed live section.
Guarded ImaxStreams HLS resolution against ad/image segments and invalid media, with candidate fallback to prevent audio-only or black-screen playback.
